sources.citation: [Ferlus, Michel; ed. Alexis Michaud]. 2024. Bibliography of Michel Ferlus. JSEALS 17.1: xxx-xxxv. hdl:10524/52525.
sources.note: Bibliographic: confirms 1974f 'La langue ong: mutations consonantiques et transphonologisations', ASEMI 5.1:113-20 (no HAL deposit), plus 1971b BSLP 66.1:389-403 'Simplification des groupes consonantiques dans deux dialectes austroasiens du Sud-Laos' and 1972b ASEMI 3.2:31-49 'Notes sur les dialectes austroasiens du Sud-Laos' (no HAL links).

sources.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan. 2017. The historical phonology of Kriang, a Katuic language. JSEALS 10.1: 114-139. hdl:10524/52402.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: For Kriang [ngt] (same Ta'oi subgroup), p.117: 'In disyllabic words, the second syllable, or the main syllable, is stressed and equivalent in its phonotactics to monosyllables. The unstressed first syllable of a disyllabic word, or the presyllable, is deficient...'. Cites Ferlus 1974 on Ong only for glottalised final sonorants (p.126). Not a statement about Ong-Ir.

sources.citation: L-Thongkum, Theraphan. 2002. A brief look at thirteen Mon-Khmer languages of Xekong province, southern Laos. In R. S. Bauer (ed.), Collected papers on Southeast Asian and Pacific languages, 95-108. Pacific Linguistics 530.
sources.note: Ong/Ir not among the 13 languages; p.101 merely names a 'Yir-Ong-Ta Oih or Katang-Ta Oih group of the East Katuic sub-branch'. Nothing on Ong-Ir stress.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1996. Évolution vers le monosyllabisme dans quelques langues de l'Asie du Sud-Est. Communication, Société de Linguistique de Paris. 7 pp. HAL halshs-00927456.
sources.note: Areal generalisation only (pp.1-2): in SE Asian 'quasi-dissyllabes' Cp(v)-CiV(Cf), 'La présyllabe a un système consonantique réduit, elle ne comporte pas de voyelle phonologique et elle est, en général, non-accentuée' (examples Khmu, Khmer). Ong not mentioned.

sources.citation: van der Haak, Feikje. 1993. Ta'uaih phonology and orthography: a preliminary statement. Mon-Khmer Studies 22: 257-264.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sister variety Upper Ta'oih [tth], not Ong-Ir. Section F 'Presyllables': presyllable vowel /a/ non-contrastive in quality; types Ca, CaC (Car- etc.). No explicit stress statement (scanned grep stress/accent = 0).

sources.citation: Diffloth, Gérard. 1982. Registres, dévoisement, timbres vocaliques: leur histoire en katouique. Mon-Khmer Studies 11: 47-82.
sources.note: Proto-Katuic vocalism and registers; Ong forms (from Ferlus 1974) appear only in cognate sets pp.27-33. No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1979. Formation des registres et mutations consonantiques dans les langues mon-khmer. Mon-Khmer Studies 8: 1-76.
sources.note: Ch.15 (pp.31-33) is devoted to Ong (citing his 1974 ASEMI paper): 'ton glottal' vs 'ton normal' (constrictive register), final stops > glottalised nasals (Tableau 14), Ong~Souei correspondences, Ong closer to Ta-oy/Ngeq/Katang. No statement about accent/stress anywhere in the Ong discussion (scanned grep accent/présyllabe/atone: only irrelevant hits). p.4 notes examples are chosen among monosyllables because disyllables undergo syntagmatic changes.

sources.citation: Huffman, Franklin E. 1971. Field notebook 21, 'Phonetic & Phonemic Lists Book II': Souei, Ir, Ta-Oi, Mankong, Katang. Huffman Papers, SEAlang Archives.
sources.note: p.1 informant metadata only (Sakorn Hongkeo, In, age 22, Ban Phakha, Tasseng Huay Pa Ai, Muang Saravane). Wordlists; not fetched sources in full; no prose on stress expected.

sources.citation: Huffman, Franklin E. 1971. Field notebook 27, 'Analysis: Ir' (informant Sakorn Hongkeo, 'In' /yiir/ [dyiir], Saravane). Franklin E. Huffman Papers, SEAlang Archives. Handwritten, 20 spreads.
sources.note: Nothing. p.16 (only prose page): consonant/final/vowel inventories, glottalized vs plain vowel contrast, homorganic preocclusion before final nasals, lax voiced stops in nasal environment, Cr-/Cl- clusters slightly aspirated, 'a certain amount of alternation between Crə- and Cər- in presyllables'. Remaining pages are rhyme-sorted vocabulary and rhyme charts (viewed pp.1,2,7,11-20). No statement on stress/accent placement.

sources.citation: Pangloss Collection (CNRS-LACITO), corpus 'Ong': 'Ong vocabulary', researcher Michel Ferlus, speaker Kham Hou, recorded 1969-03-21, 3 min 31 s, audio, untranscribed.
